description: Renovate for scalable-machine-runner (docs/ci.md, 'Pinned versions'). The Renovate GitHub App of the organization runs it. Every pin of the repository has a manager below: image digests, tool versions, PortableGit, Kata, Node.js and the Go modules.

customManagers.description: Every image reference that carries a digest, in any file: name[:tag]@sha256:<digest> (.circleci/*.yml, the stack files, ci/ and the tests, the docs, and the Dockerfiles, among them proxy/Dockerfile with the Go builder and the distroless base of the token proxy image). The stack default ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy:edge is a tag with no digest, so Renovate leaves it; a release bundle pins its own digest (ci/release.sh)

A version after a '# renovate: datasource=... depName=... [extractVersion=...]' comment: the tools of .circleci/continue.yml (Hugo, lychee, the CircleCI CLI) and of ci/*.sh (git-cliff, cosign, crane, gh, Go, govulncheck)
yamllint, installed with pip in the lint-yaml job
Kata Containers, downloaded by linux/tests/microvm.sh with its SHA-256 value
PortableGit, pinned in the Windows runner-distributor (ReleaseTag; Version and Sha256 sit next to it)
7-Zip (7zr.exe), pinned in the Windows runner-distributor with its SHA-256 value
Node.js of the Windows example image, pinned with its SHA-256 value

packageRules.description: Images that carry a digest in a stack file are what users run: a new digest is a fix and makes a release.
Images of the CI jobs, the e2e and the tests.

The base images of the token proxy image (distroless static in proxy/Dockerfile, the Nano Server digests of ci/Build-ProxyImage.ps1) are inside what users run. A new digest is a fix, so that it makes a release: with the default ci(deps) type cliff.toml skips it, and the published image keeps stale base layers until an unrelated feat or fix lands. This rule comes after 'CI images' and before 'Go toolchain', which still wins for the golang builder image.
The tools that the CI jobs download. Most come with a SHA-256 value (see the checksum rule below).
The Windows distributor downloads PortableGit and 7zr.exe on every node: shipped, so a fix.

One Go version for the proxy build (golang image of proxy/Dockerfile, ci/build-proxy.sh and proxy-test, the Go tarball of the release job) and the docs site (cimg/go). The proxy image is shipped, so a fix.
The lychee image and the lychee binary of the docs site move together.
The Hextra theme of the docs site (site/go.mod, site/go.sum).
The go directive of a go.mod is the oldest Go that can build the module: change it by hand.

cimg/base is the stock image of the stack: its tag (2026.10) is named in the stack files, the tests and the docs. Renovate refreshes the digest of the tag; a new tag is a deliberate change of every file that names it.
The tag of the e2e sweeper image names the runner build (3.1.12-...). It moves with the runner binary of ci/E2E-Host.ps1, by hand.
The Windows example image stays on Node.js 24 (an LTS line). A new line is a decision.
A major version needs a decision: Renovate waits for the approval on the Dependency Dashboard.

These downloads are pinned with a SHA-256 value that Renovate cannot compute. The pull request changes the version only, so its CI fails on the checksum until a person replaces the value. The label and the note flag the pull request.
prBodyNotes: **The SHA-256 value must change too.** Renovate updates the version only and cannot compute the checksum. Download the new asset, take its checksum from the release page (or compute it), replace the value next to the version, and push to this branch. Where is it: docs/releasing.md ('Pinned tools') and docs/ci.md ('Pinned versions'). For PortableGit also set `Version` (X.Y.Z.N for the tag vX.Y.Z.windows.N), then run `ci/config-names.sh --write`.
